This document outlines the 
major maintenance procedures P1, which must 
be performed every five years as indicated by Y5 in the title block.

The
low pressure steam turbine by-pass valve is a station for reduction the steam 
pressure and temperature outlets from the main steam of low pressure steam 
boiler to very low pressure and temperature which be able to get in the 
condenser.

The first draft 
is initiated by eng. Mohamed Abdel Azeem, tested by eng. Essam Darwish, reviewed 
by eng. Ahmed Fathy, revised by EDEPC inspection and quality control eng 
Samir Abd El Gilil; approved by general 
director eng. Mohamed Anan and accepted by 
eng. Mohamed Elsarrag head sector of 
Demiatta PS.

This document accepted by eng. Samir Abd El Gilil; 
 EDEPC inspection & quality control general director, MPIS coordinator, and certified by accountant Mahmoud Soliman: 
 EDEPC admin & financial inspection & quality control's general director, and 
 supervisor of inspection & quality control's head sector.

Before disassembly, you must measure the by-pass 
 stroke and record it.

items: Disconnect all electrical connections.
Disconnect all hydraulic and pneumatic connections.
Plug all opening immediately.

Check the alignment between the actuator and the 
 valve stem.

Remove stem coupling between actuator and valve 
 stem.
Remove the actuator by the crane.

Insert a cylindrical pin in the hole underneath the 
 stem thread to prevent the stem from sliding through the stuffing box when the 
 bonnet is removed.
Remove the gland nut (16).

Remove the locking ring (17) and then the gland bush 
 (15).
Loosen and remove bolts (22), and lift off the yoke.

Loosen the bolts (21) in the cover plate (18), and 
 lower bonnet (7) into the valve body.
Remove bolts (21) and cover plate (18).

Remove segment ring (19) by driving through the four 
 holes in the valve body with a mandrel.

Pull the complete valve bonnet out of the valve body 
 by means of hoist.
Remove the plug from the bonnet.
Remove the stuffing box (14) in case of leakage.
Remove the stem guide (8) from the stem if required.

Unscrew all bolts (5.1) and packings (5.2), remove 
 flange (5.3).

Loosen and remove nozzle holder (5), spacer ring 
 (5.4) and packing (5.5) by mounting one of bolts (5.1) in the center hole of 
 the nozzle holder and pull out the nozzle holder.

Release the locking of the nozzle (4) by bending back the lock washer (5.6) 
 and unscrew the nozzle.

Inspect the cracks in the valve interior. If there, remove them by grinding 
 and recheck with fluid penetrate test (the limit of
 cracks is 3 mm).

Remove by lapping with cast iron disc any small impressions in the seat 
 sealing surface resulting from clamped-in foreign particles.

Check corrosion inside the valve. If there, remove it by cleaning with no 
 corrosive products or by lapping with cast iron disc.

Inspect the valve seat, if there is any damages or cracks, retreat it by 
 grinding or machining.
Replace the valve seat if it cannot be reconditioning.
Check the valve bonnet for damages and treat it by grinding or machining.
Inspect packing (13) and replace it if required.
Replace the stuffing box (14) in case of leakage.
Replace the stem guide (8) if it is required.
Put a new gasket (6) in the spray nozzle.
Replace the packing (5.5) in the spray nozzle if it is required.
Clean all parts before assembly.
Change the plug.

Rub all sliding surfaces carefully with a cloth containing 
 suitable lubricant 
 (Molycote).
Install the plug (12) in bonnet (7).
Install the stem guide (8) in bonnet (7).

Insert new stem packing rings (14).
 ►Do not overfill gland with packing rings. Leave at least height of one ring 
 free to accept gland bush (15).

Insert gland bush (15), gland nut (16) and snap ring (17). Tighten gland nut 
 slightly.
 ► Do not over tighten the gland nut.

Secure stem from dropping through packing box by inserting a pin through the 
 hole in the stem.

Lift the complete bonnet assembly with the stem / plug and slide it carefully 
 into the valve body.

Inspect pressure seal gasket.
 ►Be sure that the stem / plug sets accurately on the valve seat.
Insert spacer ring (20) and segment (19).
Mount cover plate (18).
Screw the bolts (21).
Mount the actuator yoke by means of bolts (22) and tighten them.

Assemble the nozzle (4) and nozzle holder (5), secure the nozzle with spacer 
 ring (5.6)
Put a new gasket (6) on nozzle holder (5) and insert nozzle stud (5.7)

Replace packing (5.5), mount them together with spacer ring (5.4) and fit 
 flange (5.3) with bolts (5.1).
Install the actuator of the valve.
Check the alignment between actuator and valve stem.
Tight the coupling bolts firmly.
Mount the hydraulic and pneumatic connections.
Mount the electrical connections.

Introduction
This document outlines the 
major maintenance procedures P1, which must 
be performed every five years as indicated by Y5 in the title block.
The
low pressure steam turbine by-pass valve is a station for reduction the steam 
pressure and temperature outlets from the main steam of low pressure steam 
boiler to very low pressure and temperature which be able to get in the 
condenser.
Technical Specifications
Manufacturer | : | BTG Kalle 
 Sweden.
Type | : | VLR 200T.
Medium | : | Steam
Inlet Pressure | : | 4 bars.
Outlet Pressure | : | 2.5 bars.
Inlet Temperature | : | 185 C.
Outlet Temperature | : | 175 C.
Actuator | : | Hydraulic.
Dimensions (plug 
 stroke) | : | (200 
 160) mm.

is initiated by eng. Mohamed Abdel Azeem, tested by eng. Essam Darwish, reviewed 
by eng. Ahmed Fathy, revised by EDEPC inspection and quality control eng 
Samir Abd El Gilil; approved by general

Demiatta PS.

 supervisor of inspection & quality control's head sector.
Safety Precaution
A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff should carry the 
 suitable safety category
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required
Wear safety helmets, shoes, earplug and gloves pairs etc.
Shut down the unit.
Isolate the by-pass valve mechanically and 
 electrically.
Tools and Equipment
Complete maintenance tool set.
Special tools for turbine.
Spray.
Wires for lifting.
Cleaning articles.
Filler.
Work to be Carried out
Before disassembly, you must measure the by-pass 
 stroke and record it.
Disassembly
Disconnect all electrical connections.
Disconnect all hydraulic and pneumatic connections.
Plug all opening immediately.
Check the alignment between the actuator and the 
 valve stem.
Remove stem coupling between actuator and valve 
 stem.
Remove the actuator by the crane.
Insert a cylindrical pin in the hole underneath the 
 stem thread to prevent the stem from sliding through the stuffing box when the 
 bonnet is removed.
Remove the gland nut (16).
Remove the locking ring (17) and then the gland bush 
 (15).
Loosen and remove bolts (22), and lift off the yoke.
Loosen the bolts (21) in the cover plate (18), and 
 lower bonnet (7) into the valve body.
Remove bolts (21) and cover plate (18).
Remove segment ring (19) by driving through the four 
 holes in the valve body with a mandrel.
Pull the complete valve bonnet out of the valve body 
 by means of hoist.
Remove the plug from the bonnet.
Remove the stuffing box (14) in case of leakage.
Remove the stem guide (8) from the stem if required.
Unscrew all bolts (5.1) and packings (5.2), remove 
 flange (5.3).
Loosen and remove nozzle holder (5), spacer ring 
 (5.4) and packing (5.5) by mounting one of bolts (5.1) in the center hole of 
 the nozzle holder and pull out the nozzle holder.
Release the locking of the nozzle (4) by bending back the lock washer (5.6) 
 and unscrew the nozzle.
Inspection
Inspect the cracks in the valve interior. If there, remove them by grinding 
 and recheck with fluid penetrate test (the limit of
 cracks is 3 mm).
Remove by lapping with cast iron disc any small impressions in the seat 
 sealing surface resulting from clamped-in foreign particles.
Check corrosion inside the valve. If there, remove it by cleaning with no 
 corrosive products or by lapping with cast iron disc.
Inspect the valve seat, if there is any damages or cracks, retreat it by 
 grinding or machining.
Replace the valve seat if it cannot be reconditioning.
Check the valve bonnet for damages and treat it by grinding or machining.
Inspect packing (13) and replace it if required.
Replace the stuffing box (14) in case of leakage.
Replace the stem guide (8) if it is required.
Put a new gasket (6) in the spray nozzle.
Replace the packing (5.5) in the spray nozzle if it is required.
Clean all parts before assembly.
Change the plug.
Rub all sliding surfaces carefully with a cloth containing 
 suitable lubricant 
 (Molycote).
Assembly
Install the plug (12) in bonnet (7).
Install the stem guide (8) in bonnet (7).
Insert new stem packing rings (14).
 ►Do not overfill gland with packing rings. Leave at least height of one ring 
 free to accept gland bush (15).
Insert gland bush (15), gland nut (16) and snap ring (17). Tighten gland nut 
 slightly.
 ► Do not over tighten the gland nut.
Secure stem from dropping through packing box by inserting a pin through the 
 hole in the stem.
Lift the complete bonnet assembly with the stem / plug and slide it carefully 
 into the valve body.
Inspect pressure seal gasket.
 ►Be sure that the stem / plug sets accurately on the valve seat.
Insert spacer ring (20) and segment (19).
Mount cover plate (18).
Screw the bolts (21).
Mount the actuator yoke by means of bolts (22) and tighten them.
Assemble the nozzle (4) and nozzle holder (5), secure the nozzle with spacer 
 ring (5.6)
Put a new gasket (6) on nozzle holder (5) and insert nozzle stud (5.7)
Replace packing (5.5), mount them together with spacer ring (5.4) and fit 
 flange (5.3) with bolts (5.1).
Install the actuator of the valve.
Check the alignment between actuator and valve stem.
Tight the coupling bolts firmly.
Mount the hydraulic and pneumatic connections.
Mount the electrical connections.
